instructions:
### ROLE ###
You maintain a small, growing set of CONCEPT SCHEMES (entity categories) for a knowledge registry built from cybersecurity incident reports. A group of entities extracted from several reports has just been found to be close to each other and far from every existing scheme. Decide whether the group is a genuinely new scheme or an alias of an existing one, and name it.

### EXISTING SCHEMES ###
- Software Product: A commercial, open-source, or proprietary software application, suite, tool, or component used for computing tasks.
- Software Vendor: A company or organization that develops, publishes, or sells software or technology products and services.
- Security Advisory: An official public notice or document providing information, remediation, or patches regarding cybersecurity vulnerabilities or threats.
- Security Vulnerability: A flaw or weakness in software, hardware, or system design that can be exploited to compromise security.
- Operating System: System software that manages computer hardware, software resources, and provides common services for computer programs.
- Country: A distinct sovereign nation or geopolitical state entity.
- Government Agency: An official public authority, ministry, department, or state institution operating within a national or local government.
- Software Update: A software release, patch, or package designed to fix vulnerabilities, resolve bugs, or improve computer programs and operating systems.

### THE GROUP ###
Each line is one entity with the description written at extraction time:
- *.gov.ua [internet domain] — The second-level domain zone designated for Ukrainian government entities.
- cautionphenomenon[.]co[.]kr [internet domain] — A malicious internet domain hosting a phishing landing page targeting user credentials.
- microsoft.com [internet domain] — The official domain name of Microsoft Corporation.

### RULES ###
- A scheme is a KIND of entity (e.g. "Hacker group", "Malware family", "Software product", "Government body", "Internet domain", "Country"), never a role in an incident and never a single entity.
- Return `"verdict": "alias-of"` with `"target"` set to an existing scheme's label when the group is the same kind as that scheme (different wording, same meaning). Judge by MEANING of the descriptions, not by surface words.
- Return `"verdict": "new"` when no existing scheme covers the group. Then give:
  - `prefLabel`: a short English noun phrase, 1–3 words, singular, Title Case (e.g. "Malware Family").
  - `definition`: one sentence, at most 25 words, stating what belongs to the scheme, general enough to hold across reports.
  - `altLabels`: 0–3 alternative English labels.
- If the group mixes clearly different kinds, name the kind of the MAJORITY and list the minority entity names in `outliers`.
- If uncertain between alias and new, prefer `new`: an extra scheme can be merged later; a wrong merge cannot be undone cheaply.

### OUTPUT ###
A single raw JSON object, no markdown fences, no commentary:
{ "verdict": "new" | "alias-of", "target": "<existing label or null>", "prefLabel": "...", "definition": "...", "altLabels": [...], "outliers": [...] }
text: Decide and name the group now.
response: {"verdict": "new", "target": null, "prefLabel": "Internet Domain", "definition": "A unique identification string used to locate and access network resources and systems on the Internet.", "altLabels": ["Domain Name", "Web Domain"], "outliers": []}
